Subject: Initial sizing questions + quick-fit checklist for Dedicated capacity

Hi Kate,

Great to connect yesterday — thanks for the context on the POC and the throughput targets. To get a tight Dedicated SKU recommendation (H100 vs A100 vs L4) and a pragmatic ops runbook, could you confirm the following items? I attached a one-page questionnaire and a starter CSV with the fields we use to estimate pool mixes.

Quick asks:
- Target steady-state QPS and peak QPS (and expected peak windows).
- Average prompt tokens / average response tokens (or example prompt/response sizes).
- P95 latency SLO (e.g. <300ms, <500ms).
- % of calls that require long context (>8k tokens) vs short (<=2k tokens).
- Models you plan to run in production and the set you’ll test in canary (names & sizes).
- Any hard constraints: air-gapped, private VPC, KMS requirements, or procurement/contract windows.

High-level notes on tradeoffs (so we’re aligned):
- H100: best for large-context, large models (70B+), highest peak throughput per slot for heavy attention workloads; higher unit cost.
- A100: good midline for 7B–30B/13B families when memory is needed but extreme context isn’t constant.
- L4: cost-efficient, lowest-latency for short-context/quantized variants; limited for 70B or 64k contexts.

If you can send answers by EOD tomorrow we’ll sketch a Dedicated pool proposal and an ops playbook (canary, fallback, caching).

Thanks —
Priyom Das

Hi Priyom,

Thanks — answers below inline. Also tagging our engineering lead (we'll introduce formally in the next thread).

- Steady-state QPS: 120 QPS. Peak: 300 QPS for short bursts (5–10 minutes during business hours).
- Tokens: avg prompt ~60 tokens, avg response ~120 tokens (so ~180 tokens per cycle).
- P95 latency SLO: target <500ms for production; <300ms preferred for priority customers.
- Context mix: ~70% short (<=2k), ~25% medium (2–16k), ~5% long (>16k). We have a small set of workflows that need 64k context for doc ingestion.
- Models: will run a tuned 13B sequence (internal finetune), evaluating Llama-2-70B for longer-context experiments. Canary will include 13B and a quantized 13B-L4 option.
- Constraints: VPC; procurement timeline — we'd like committed Dedicated by end of October.

Can you provide a recommended pool mix and a canary/fallback approach? We need a rough cost/latency tradeoff to take to finance next week.

—Kate

Quick analysis / recommendation (high level):

Observations from their inputs:
- 120 steady QPS * 180 tokens = ~21.6k tokens/sec sustained. Peak 300 QPS => ~54k tokens/sec.
- Long-context calls are rare (5%) but require 64k headroom for a small set of workflows.
- Models: 13B finetune will be dominant; 70B will be experimental.

Recommended Dedicated pool (initial commit):
- H100 (flavor: H100 80GB): 6 nodes — purpose: run 70B experiments + the 64k-context workflows (sticky routing). H100 handles memory-bound long-context and larger attention compute.
- A100 (80GB): 18 nodes — purpose: primary 13B finetuned production traffic and mid-sized models; balances memory and cost.
- L4 (48GB equivalent vGPU): 36 nodes — purpose: cost-efficient, low-latency for the 70% short-context workload, quantized 13B-L4 fallback, and embeddings.

Rationale and sizing math (approx):
- A100 per-slot (13B FP16/quantized) can serve ~6–8 concurrent requests at our 500ms target with batching; L4 can serve ~20 concurrent small prompts at <300ms due to small kernels and quantization. H100 slots needed only for long-context or 70B; 6 H100s give enough concurrent capacity for the expected 5% long-context with headroom for canary.
- Headroom: this mix targets ~2x headroom for steady-state on L4/A100 combined and ~3x for H100 on long-context bursts. Peaks routed first to L4/A100 (cheap) — fall back to H100 only for models that require it.

Operational recommendations (ops runbook bullets):
1) Canary plan (2 weeks):
   - Week 0: Provision 30% of proposed pool (2 H100, 6 A100, 12 L4).
   - Run canary traffic with traffic mirror (10% of prod) and validate p95 & token-cost metric.
   - Smoke tests: cold-starts, KV cache hit-rates, autoscaling triggers.
2) Routing policy:
   - Model pinning: 13B → A100 primary, L4 quantized variant as fallback.
   - Long-context requests tagged and routed to H100 pool by policy; include strict token cutoff to avoid unexpected FATAL OOM behavior.
3) Caching & batching:
   - Enable prefix/KV cache for repeated chat sessions (expected >20% cacheable).
   - Aggressive batching for A100 during non-latency-critical flows.
4) Fallbacks:
   - If A100 saturation >85% for >2m, overflow to L4 quantized for short-context flows; for long-context flows overflow to smaller chunked inference on H100 or degrade to a cached summary.
5) SLA & SLO guardrails:
   - Autoscale thresholds: scale-up at 65% average slot utilization sustained for 90s.
   - Alerting: token-rate + p95 breaching -> immediate ops paging and automatic scaled burst to reserved spare slots.

Attachments: ops_runbook_v2.pdf, cost_vs_latency_table.csv (contains token/s and cost estimates per SKU).

If you want I can refine exact node counts based on their VM/GPU SKU pricing and whether they prefer per-hour or monthly reserved pricing.

—Aditya

Hi Kate — thank you for the fast turnaround. We reviewed with our infra team and recommend the following Dedicated commitment and phased plan to meet your SLOs while keeping unit costs reasonable. See attached runbook and cost table.

Summary recommendation (initial committed pool):
- H100 (80GB): 6 nodes — reserved for 70B experiments and the small set of 64k-context workflows.
- A100 (80GB): 18 nodes — primary workhorse for the 13B finetuned model (production).
- L4 (vGPU slices / equivalent 48GB): 36 nodes — handle the 70% short-context steady-state traffic and quantized fallbacks.

Why this mix?
- Meets steady-state 120 QPS with ~2x headroom across the L4+A100 blended pool for short & medium context.
- H100 capacity isolated for long-context and 70B experiments to avoid noisy-neighbor performance regressions.
- Cost control via L4 for the majority of cheap short requests; A100 handles memory-heavy 13B work with predictable latency.

Phased launch plan (timeline to meet end-of-October commit):
1) Canary (2 weeks): provision 30% capacity: 2 H100 / 6 A100 / 12 L4; mirror 10% prod traffic; validate p95 and failover.
2) Scale to 70% after successful canary (1 week): 4 H100 / 12 A100 / 25 L4.
3) Full commit by Oct 28: 6 H100 / 18 A100 / 36 L4 (as above).

Operational highlights:
- Routing: model pinning + token-aware routing; long-context tagged to H100.
- Caching: prefix/KV cache recommended for stateful chat; expected >15% token savings.
- Fallbacks: quantized 13B on L4 for short requests; degrade long-context to summary+chunking if H100 capacity is constrained.

Estimated next steps for procurement:
- We can provide a pricing sheet (monthly reserved vs committed hourly) and an SOW for Dedicated. Aditya attached a cost vs latency table — that will help finance choose the reserved mix.

Attachments: ops_runbook_v2.pdf, cost_vs_latency_table.csv

If you want, we can run a quick 30-minute call Tuesday to walk finance through the cost table and the canary plan. Does 10am PT work?

Warmly,
